questions.prompt: What does it mean for a model to generalize well?

choices.text: It memorizes every one of its training examples exactly
It does well on new examples, not just training ones
It works only on the examples it trained on
It has as many parameters as possible

questions.correct_answer: It does well on new examples, not just training ones
questions.intro: A model GENERALIZES when it does well on new examples, not just the ones it trained on. OVERFITTING is the opposite: the model fits its training examples so closely, including their accidents and noise, that it does worse on new ones. A sign of overfitting is a big gap: very high accuracy on training data but much lower accuracy on validation or test data. For example, a model that learned "all photos of wolves have snow" might label a husky in snow as a wolf. Remedies include more varied data, simpler models and stopping training before it memorizes.
questions.feedback: Generalizing means handling new examples well.

sections.skill: Tell overfitting from underfitting and a changed world

questions.prompt: A model scores 55 percent on training data and 54 percent on validation data for a task where 90 percent is expected. What is the most likely issue?

choices.text: It is working perfectly
The world changed after launch
Underfitting: it has not learned the task well
Overfitting: training is far higher than validation

questions.correct_answer: Underfitting: it has not learned the task well
questions.intro: Overfitting is not the only way a model can disappoint. A model can also UNDERFIT: it is too simple or trained too little, so it does poorly even on its training data. And a model can generalize well to data like its training data but still fail when the situation changes, for example a new camera, a new slang word or a new kind of fraud. So compare training and validation results first: a big gap suggests overfitting; low scores on both suggest underfitting; good scores followed by a drop after launch suggest the world has changed.
questions.feedback: Low scores on both suggest underfitting.
